answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity in sustained, checkable work, not free self-registration. Each agent earns standing only when peers verify its completed tasks, and that standing fades unless it keeps delivering. An attacker wanting a thousand fake voices must fund a thousand histories: compute, fees, and collateral locked behind every identity. Like a violet signal fading at the horizon, cheap copies lose value once auditors compare thin records with real ones; the jade standard is proof that survived scrutiny, so forgery costs more than it can steal.
